title: Analyses of the mechanism and therapeutic targets of senescence related genes in ischemic stroke with multi-omics approach

evidence_spans.quote: We developed a multi-omics framework
Ischemic stroke (IS) affects 11 million people annually
investigate senescence-associated gene regulation in IS
senescence-related genes as promising biomarkers and therapeutic targets for IS
We developed a multi-omics framework

scope_reviewer.uncertainty_reason: The report analyzes senescence-associated/aging-related gene labels in ischemic stroke, but does not explicitly analyze a senescent state or another aging construct itself.
scope_reviewer.concise_rationale: This is an empirical biological study. Its explicit multi-omics claim is accompanied by transcriptomic DEG analysis, but no second currently used molecular layer is named; aging relevance remains unresolved because the stated targets and outcomes are ischemic-stroke biomarkers and therapies.

evidence_spans.quote: machine learning-driven Weighted Gene Co-expression Network Analysis (WGCNA)
A strong positive correlation (r = 0.72, p < 0.001) between NFE2L2 and PTGS2 expression

causal_design_reviewer.concise_rationale: The report applies differential-expression, network, profiling, and correlation analyses, without an intervention, genetic instrument, mediation analysis, or directed causal model.

adjudication.uncertainty_reason: The abstract labels genes as senescence-associated or aging-related but does not explicitly measure, induce, reverse, or compare cellular senescence or another aging construct. It claims a multi-omics framework while naming only DEG-based expression analysis as a molecular layer.
adjudication.concise_rationale: This original study analyzes ischemic-stroke datasets and reports transcriptomic differential-expression and noncausal network/correlation analyses. Aging relevance and multi-omics status remain unresolved from the title and abstract.
